notes.meaning: Moses was tending sheep for his father-in-law Jethro in the desert near Mount Horeb. After forty years of royal comfort in Egypt, Moses had spent forty humble years as a shepherd, learning patience and contentment. God often prepares His servants through quiet, ordinary labor before calling them to great tasks.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern scholars view the text as a combination of distinct older written sources rather than a single unified narrative.

notes.meaning: The Angel of the Lord appeared to Moses inside a thorny bush that burned with fire without burning up. The unconsumed bush pictured God's people suffering in Egypt's painful oppression, preserved from destruction because God was with them. The Angel who spoke was the Lord Himself, showing His glory and protection.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Orthodox tradition sees the unburnt bush as a picture of the Virgin Mary, who gave birth to Christ without losing her virginity.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Roman Catholic liturgy also interprets the bush burning without being consumed as a symbol of Mary conceiving Jesus while remaining a virgin.

notes.meaning: Moses was amazed by what he saw and decided to step aside from his path to find out why the bush did not burn away. God used this desert wonder to capture his full attention. When God reaches out to us, He expects us to stop and listen rather than walk on by.

When Moses walked over to look, God called him by name twice from inside the bush, and Moses answered, 'Here I am.' Calling his name twice showed urgent love and summoned him into direct conversation with God. A true call from the Lord reaches the heart and makes a person ready to listen and obey.

God told Moses to stop where he was and take off his sandals because God's presence made that place holy. Taking off shoes was an ancient sign of respect, showing humble submission and human unworthiness before God. We must approach God with reverent awe and clean hearts.

God announced Himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the founding fathers of Israel. Because God spoke as their living God, this showed that these fathers were still alive with Him beyond the grave. Terrified by God's holiness and glory, Moses hid his face in fear.

The Lord assured Moses that He had clearly seen the misery of Israel and heard their cries under cruel slave masters. God was deeply aware of their pain, even though their suffering had lasted for decades. God knows every hidden sorrow of His people and is never deaf to their prayers.

God declared that He had come down to rescue Israel from Egypt and lead them into Canaan, a wide and fertile land. Describing the land as flowing with milk and honey meant it was rich and full of good things. When God frees people from bondage, He brings them into His abundant blessings.

Israel's cry had reached heaven, and the Lord had witnessed how brutally the Egyptians were mistreating them. Their suffering moved God to step forward as their rescuer and judge. Earthly rulers are never above God's justice when they harm the weak.

God commanded Moses to go to Pharaoh and lead the Israelites out of Egypt. Even though God had promised to deliver them Himself, He chose to accomplish His rescue through a human messenger. God often uses ordinary people to carry out His great works.

Moses shrank back and asked how a simple shepherd could possibly confront Pharaoh or lead an entire nation to freedom. Forty years earlier he had been eager and self-confident, but now he felt completely weak and unfit for the task. True humility begins by recognizing our own limitations when God calls us.

God answered Moses not by flattering his ability, but by promising, 'I will surely be with you.' He gave Moses a sign that after the exodus, the whole nation would worship God right here on this mountain. God's presence is all we need to overcome our deepest weaknesses.

Moses asked what name he should give when the Israelites asked which God had sent him. Living in Egypt among many false gods, the people would want to know the true character and authority of the God who promised them deliverance. Moses wanted to be prepared with clear instructions before speaking to them.

God revealed His name as 'I AM WHO I AM,' commanding Moses to tell the Israelites that 'I AM' had sent him. This name reveals that God exists on His own, has no beginning or end, never changes, and faithfully keeps His word. He alone is the source of all life and being.

differ.view: Some Reformed teachers emphasize that the name primarily promises God's active, saving presence with His people rather than just defining His abstract eternal being.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars see the name as derived from the verb for being, pointing to God's continuous and active presence throughout history.

notes.meaning: God told Moses to identify Him as the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, establishing this covenant name as His remembrance forever. A covenant is a sacred agreement, and this title assured the people that God's ancient promises were still active. God never forgets His promises to His people.

Moses was directed to gather the elders, the recognized leaders of Israel, to announce that God had visited them and seen their misery. Starting with the elders ensured that the nation would be properly guided and united in hope. God never overlooks His people, even when help seems long delayed.

God reaffirmed His solemn promise to lift Israel out of Egyptian slavery and settle them in the rich land of Canaan. Describing it as flowing with milk and honey assured them of fruitful abundance after years of grinding poverty. What God promises to do in His counsel will certainly come to pass.

God promised that the elders would listen to Moses, and they were to ask Pharaoh for permission to take a three-day journey into the wilderness to offer sacrifices. This modest and reasonable request tested the king's heart without laying out God's full plan at once. When people reject God's mild requests, their stubborn rebellion is laid bare.

God warned Moses in advance that the king of Egypt would stubbornly refuse their request unless forced by a mighty hand. Knowing this ahead of time protected Moses from losing heart when the king resisted. God is never surprised or thwarted by the stubbornness of human rulers.

The Lord announced that He would stretch out His hand and strike Egypt with miraculous wonders until Pharaoh finally let the people go. When proud kings refuse to obey God's word, His power will break their pride through judgment. No human power can successfully resist the hand of God.

God promised that He would cause the Egyptians to show goodwill toward the Israelites so that they would not leave empty-handed. God has complete power over human hearts and can turn harsh oppressors into generous givers. God faithfully provides for His people when the time for their freedom arrives.

Israelite women were instructed to ask their Egyptian neighbors for silver, gold, and clothing, carrying away the wealth of Egypt. This was not dishonesty or borrowing without returning, but fair payment for generations of unpaid slave labor. God balances every account and sees that the oppressed receive justice.
